title: Strongly coupled atom-cavity systems under boundary modulation: simulating gravitational-wave effects
authors: Patryk Michalski, Jerzy Paczos, Navdeep Arya, Magdalena Zych
abstract: One of the proposed platforms in which both quantum and general relativistic effects can become observable is an atom interacting with the electromagnetic field in a gravitational-wave background. The periodic modulation of field modes induced by variations of the spacetime metric modifies the atomic emission spectrum. Notably, the temporal modulation of the mode-frequency induced by a plane gravitational wave can be simulated through modulated boundary conditions, such as moving cavity mirrors. We analyze the impact of this modulation on atom-field interactions in the strong atom-cavity coupling regime, where Rabi oscillations occur. We show analytically that the modulation is resonantly enhanced, leading to measurable imprints in the atomic transition probability. This establishes a realistic and experimentally accessible platform for probing analogue general relativistic effects in quantum optical systems.
summary: This paper analyzes how an atom-cavity system can simulate the effects of a gravitational wave by modulating the cavity mirrors. Using perturbation theory and multiple-scales analysis, the authors show that this modulation causes a measurable, resonantly enhanced change in the atomic transition probability. This establishes a viable quantum optical platform for testing analogue general relativistic effects.
main_problem: To establish a realistic and experimentally accessible platform for probing analogue general relativistic effects by simulating the influence of a plane gravitational wave on atom-field interactions.
main_result: The modulation induced by the gravitational wave analogue is shown to be resonantly enhanced, leading to measurable imprints in the atomic transition probability.
method: The analysis employs time-dependent perturbation theory and the multiple-scales approach to calculate the first-order correction to the atomic transition probability.
model_or_system: The system is a two-level atom strongly coupled to a single quantized mode of the electromagnetic field inside an optical cavity. The gravitational wave effect is simulated by modulating the cavity resonance frequency via time-dependent boundary conditions.
key_observables: The primary observable is the correction to the atomic emission rates or the excited-state population probability, $p_e(t)$. The classical Fisher information $I_C(t)$ is used to quantify measurement sensitivity.
important_parameters: Key parameters include the modulation amplitude $A$, the driving frequency $\omega$, and the detuning $\delta_0$. Resonance is achieved when the cavity frequency matches the modulation frequency.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the modulation is adiabatic and treats the modulation as a small perturbation to the standard Jaynes-Cummings model.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows the schematic setup involving a cavity, atom, and movable mirror. Figure 2 illustrates the frequency dependence of the probability correction, showing resonance. Figure 3 shows the classical Fisher information.
paper_structure: The paper develops the Hamiltonian, applies perturbative expansions to find the probability correction $\delta p_e(t)$, and then uses the multiple-scales method to extend the analysis to longer coherence times, culminating in the calculation of the optimal measurement time via Fisher information.
why_interesting: This work directly bridges quantum optics (cavity QED) with fundamental physics (General Relativity) by proposing a concrete, measurable analogue experiment, which is highly relevant to AMO physicists working on open quantum systems.
